Chapter 7: The Realities of Publication—Submission, Rejection, and Professionalism.
So, you’ve spent all that time honing your craft—now comes the next big hurdle: putting your work out there. I know, it can feel overwhelming, right? The world of publication is full of unknowns, and yes, the possibility of rejection. But it’s also where you’ll find real opportunities to grow, connect with others, and even validate all that effort you’ve poured into your writing.
Everything starts with submission. That means sending your stories or essays to magazines, agents, or publishers. It takes a bit of homework—figuring out who’s the right fit for your work, being patient, and always following those submission guidelines. Every time you hit send, it’s a little leap of hope. There’s a wait, sometimes a long one, and no promises about what you’ll hear back.
And then there’s rejection. Look, nobody loves it, but it’s just part of the game. Even the most famous authors have stacks of rejection letters tucked away somewhere. The secret? Don’t take it personally. Rejection doesn’t mean you’ve failed—it’s just one more step on your path. Every response, even if it’s just a form letter, is proof that you’re trying, that you’re persistent. Sometimes, you’ll even get feedback from an editor or agent, and that’s gold—use it to make your work even better.
Through all of this, professionalism matters more than you might think. Here’s what that looks like:
Respect deadlines and always stick to submission guidelines. If you get feedback—good or bad—respond graciously. Keep your communication with editors, agents, and your fellow writers clear and polite. And most importantly, keep writing and submitting, even when things don’t go your way.
Building a writing career isn’t something that happens overnight. Most of us are balancing jobs, families, and all sorts of responsibilities right alongside our creative goals. Success usually comes in small doses: maybe a story gets picked up, or you get a kind note from an editor. Those little wins build up over time, giving you confidence and momentum to keep going.
Remember, publication isn’t the finish line—it’s just a milestone along the way. Sure, it feels great to see your work in print and to know your stories are reaching readers. But the true reward? That’s in the writing itself—the daily practice, the personal growth, and the pure joy of sharing your words with the world.
